description: pulselog-panel-strict — authored through the bareloop panel (green, js)
goal: Run the type checker in strict mode with no emit and confirm zero errors in src/checks.js, confirm no new type errors in any other file under src/ against the pre-change baseline, and run the existing test suite to confirm every existing test still passes.

notes: No strict-typing script exists in the repository: package.json scripts.typecheck is "tsc --noEmit" and tsconfig.json sets strict:false (with strictNullChecks:true). The confirmed plan asks for strict mode, so both typecheck stages run the project's own script through the project's own runner with --strict appended (npm run typecheck -- --strict); the binary is never named bare.

Only src/** is inside tsc's include list, so bin/ and test/ are never type-checked by this command. "No new type errors anywhere else in src/" can only be judged for src/, and the typecheck-outside stage's ceiling is the STRICT-mode seed count, re-measured in place every run.

The target stage reads a TALLY of piped tsc error lines (pattern `error TS\d+`, no capture group, aggregate "sum") so that zero errors is a legitimate counted zero rather than an unreported number; the outside stage uses the identical parser with src/checks.js excluded, so the two stages are complementary halves of one run and are never summed into one series.

test/pulselog.test.js is the only test path named under that heading in the seed listing, but the listing does show five test files under test/ (pulselog, digest, backup, deliver, fallback); the suite is invoked once per suite stage via the project's own script (npm test -> node --test), and the executed-test count is read off the TAP `# tests` line exactly as the genre spells it. The facts object's "ℹ tests 42" was inferred; the measured executed count at seed is 67.

NOT COVERED, per the person's own words — "no any casts": none of the confirmed checks can detect an `any` cast added to satisfy the checker. The always-on no-suppressions guard carries an `any`-shaped pattern over added .js/.mjs/.cjs lines, which may catch some spellings, but that is a genre guard and I am not claiming it as coverage of this request.

NOT COVERED — "do not change what the code does": only the five existing test files run, so behaviour those tests do not exercise is not verified. Also, editing or deleting tests is not directly detectable; the tests-kept floor and suite-zero-failing-tests would catch a suite that shrank or broke, but a rewritten-and-still-passing test file would not be caught.

No TZ is set in package.json or ci.yml, and the surveyor found no documented env need, so no env override is passed. I note the residual risk: digest.test.js pins UTC instants (ANCHOR ... 'Z'), so if the harness timezone ever moved off UTC those tests could shift; they were green at seed and I did not want to invent an environment the project does not declare.

No timeout or PATH-like environment is declared by the repository, so none is passed; generous per-stage timeouts are declared because several tests spawn real 'sh' child processes and mutate process.env.PATH internally.
Every parser pattern used here is a genre-known pipe shape (tsc-error-line tally, node-test-total-count, node-test-fail-count); I composed no pattern for any tool myself.
